description: Curriculum topic bank for writing content generation, aligned with WIDA ELP levels 1–6. Topics increase in cognitive and linguistic complexity as students progress. Each level provides writing genres and task contexts appropriate for the proficiency band.

levels.complexityNote: Grade 6–8 writing tasks involving labeling, completing sentence frames, or producing 2–3 word phrases. Students reproduce words and phrases with visual support. Sentence frames are required.

topics: label parts of a plant or animal cell
complete sentences about weather using a word bank
write phrases to describe objects in an ecosystem
complete a sentence frame about a landform
label a diagram of the solar system
complete sentences naming community helpers and their jobs
label a map with country or continent names
write names of government branches and one thing each does
complete sentences about a historical figure using a word bank
label transportation types with where they travel
complete a sentence about a favorite food and why
label pictures of a school day schedule
complete a sentence about a family member using a word bank
write words to describe your home community
complete a sentence about something you learned in school

levels.complexityNote: Grade 6–8 writing tasks producing 2–4 simple sentences. Students connect ideas using basic connectors (and, because, then) with word banks and sentence frames. Some Tier-2 vocabulary introduced.

topics: describe two steps of the water cycle in sentences
write about the cause of a natural disaster
compare two animals using a sentence frame
write about what happens in a food chain
describe how a plant adapts to its environment
write about why people immigrate using a sentence frame
describe two steps of how a bill becomes a law
compare two regions of the United States
write about a historical event using a timeline
describe the job of one branch of government
write about what you did before and after school yesterday
describe a meal or food from your home culture
write about a challenge you faced and how you solved it
describe a place in your community
write about something you learned to do for the first time

levels.complexityNote: Grade 6–8 writing tasks producing one short paragraph (4–6 sentences) with a main idea and supporting details. Students use transition words and some Tier-2 academic vocabulary. Sentence frame provided as optional support.

topics: explain how photosynthesis works in a paragraph
describe the cause and effect of pollution on an ecosystem
explain the steps of the rock cycle
write about how the immune system fights infection
describe a simple machine and how it helps people
write about the causes of the American Revolution
explain what the civil rights movement accomplished
describe how checks and balances prevent abuses of power
write about the impact of westward expansion on Native Americans
explain why ancient civilizations are still important to study
write your opinion on whether school uniforms should be required
explain why a character's decision in a story was right or wrong
describe the theme of a story and support it with text evidence
write about how figurative language helps readers understand a text
explain why reading for fun is important

levels.complexityNote: Grade 6–8 writing tasks producing 2 organized paragraphs (7–10 sentences, 100–150 words). Students write reports, opinion essays, or comparative pieces with topic sentences and supporting evidence. Moderate Tier-2 vocabulary; no sentence frame.

topics: argue whether renewable energy should replace fossil fuels
explain the causes and effects of climate change using evidence
compare the pros and cons of genetic engineering in agriculture
write a report on how the immune system and vaccines work together
explain why biodiversity is essential to ecosystem health
explain the causes and consequences of World War I
compare two historical leaders and evaluate their impact
argue whether the U.S. government has done enough to protect civil rights
write about the economic effects of the Industrial Revolution
explain how immigration has shaped American culture and economy
compare two characters from different texts facing a similar conflict
argue whether social media has a positive or negative effect on teens
evaluate an author's argument: are the claims well-supported?
write about how a story's setting shapes its characters and themes
compare two news sources reporting on the same event

levels.complexityNote: Grade 6–8 writing tasks producing 3–4 paragraphs (150–250 words) with introduction, body, and conclusion. Students write research-based essays, persuasive pieces with counterarguments, and analytical comparisons. High Tier-2 and some Tier-3 vocabulary.

topics: present a researched argument on whether AI poses more benefits or risks
write a persuasive essay on expanding space exploration funding
analyze the evidence for and against mandatory vaccination policies
write a research report on the societal effects of social media algorithms
argue whether nuclear energy should be part of a clean energy strategy
analyze the long-term effects of colonialism on economic development
write a persuasive essay on whether the U.S. should reform immigration laws
compare democracy and authoritarianism using historical examples
argue whether economic inequality is a greater threat than political polarization
analyze how the Cold War continues to shape current geopolitics
analyze how a novel's narrative structure creates thematic meaning
compare the rhetorical strategies of two historical speeches
write a literary analysis of how symbolism develops theme in a text
argue whether dystopian fiction is effective social commentary
evaluate how postcolonial literature reframes historical narratives

levels.complexityNote: Grade 6–8 complex writing tasks producing 4–6 paragraphs (250–400+ words). Students write thesis-driven analytical essays, synthesize multiple sources, introduce counterarguments, and write with nuanced vocabulary and varied sentence structures.

topics: write a thesis-driven essay evaluating the ethical limits of biotechnology
synthesize sources to argue a position on geoengineering as a climate solution
analyze how neuroscience research should inform classroom teaching practices
evaluate competing scientific models and argue which has stronger evidence
write an analytical essay on the societal costs of antibiotic resistance
synthesize primary and secondary sources to argue a revisionist historical claim
write a comparative analysis of two constitutional systems
evaluate the long-term legacy of the Cold War on current international order
analyze whether the United Nations has succeeded in its founding mission
write an argument about whether economic development justifies political repression
write a thesis-driven analysis of how narrative perspective creates bias in a novel
synthesize multiple critical perspectives to argue an interpretation of a poem
analyze how a canonical text reflects and critiques its historical moment
compare the ideological assumptions embedded in two literary genres
evaluate competing scholarly arguments about a literary work's cultural significance
